assumptions.summary: Conspirators and non-conspirators are linearly separable in the selected local-feature space.
Conspirators avoid suspicious topics with outsiders and avoid irrelevant topics with accomplices.
A leader reduces direct contacts, while a non-conspirator does not know conspirator identities.
The EZ and 83-node networks are stable and share the same information-transmission mechanism.
More known-conspirator neighbors increase a node's conspiracy likelihood.
Irrelevant messages received from a known conspirator indicate an outlier.
Expert-selected words can represent suspicious semantic affinity across topics.
A criminal leader tends to send commands, so communication edges should be reversed for LeaderRank.
Known-label errors occur independently in the sensitivity stress test.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: The Summary defines an employee message network with known criminals, known non-criminals, suspicious topics, unknown individuals, and a separate leader output.
Figure 1 shows 83 people with seven known conspirators and a small known non-conspirator set embedded in a larger unlabeled network.
Directed degree, betweenness, and closeness are used with known-neighbor possession and message-topic behavior to form five features.
Topic 16 is declared wrong and discarded; Table 1 records topics among known conspirators.
All training cases come from only 15 known conspirators and non-conspirators.
Duplicate manager names are resolved by choosing the node with the larger out-degree.
The expert dictionary is set to Spanish, system, network, computer, and meeting.
Table 3 ranks 15 topics by returned resource, but the subsequent topic-4 append conflicts with its zero score.
The leader graph retains messages on known suspicious topics 7, 11, and 13, reverses edges, and adds a ground node.
Requirement 2 adds Topic 1 as suspicious and changes Chris from innocent to guilty.

dependency_graph.handoff: Five topology and message features become the logistic classifier inputs.
The classifier is evaluated and regularized through the 15 leave-one-out folds.
The base 0.27 error and missing message meaning motivate semantic diffusion.
The selected semantic topic is fed back into the logistic feature system for retraining.
Because conspiracy likelihood is not leadership, the workflow switches to a filtered LeaderRank model.
Changed labels and topics trigger a full classifier rerun followed by rank and probability sensitivity checks.

Version the topic-16 correction, duplicate-name resolution, labels, and message graph.
Report scaled features, coefficients, convergence traces, thresholds, calibration, and decision costs.
Use nested model selection, fold predictions, uncertainty, and an independent labeled test network.
Version dictionary construction, tokenization, ambiguity review, annotators, and leakage controls.
Resolve the topic-4 versus Table-3 conflict before semantic feedback.
Compare original and reversed directions, define subgraph membership, and reproduce LeaderRank convergence.
Collect independent leader labels and compare PageRank, HITS, LeaderRank, centrality, and null rankings.
Stress correlated and adversarial label errors and report intervals for tau, probabilities, and threshold crossings.
Separate rank stability, calibration stability, and action stability in before-after plots.
Evaluate external networks with domain-specific features, privacy and ethics review, runtime, and portability diagnostics.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: The Summary binds methods to reported error, rank, and limitation evidence.
Two baseline weaknesses directly motivate the hybrid strategy.
Label scarcity is met with an explicit leave-one-out design.
A base error triggers a semantic repair and same-metric rerun.
Likelihood and leadership are separated before direction-aware model adaptation.
Rank stability and probability movement are both shown rather than collapsed into one claim.

language_observations.summary: Human style is carried by dual-baseline contrast, concrete behavior-to-feature reasoning, label-scarcity-aware validation, same-metric repair, estimand correction, direction repair, table/figure reading, and qualified portability.

summary moves from task through methods to measured results and limits: Compress the decision task, assumptions, model chain, numerical checks, leader output, and transfer limits without hiding the evidence class.
two baseline weaknesses motivate a hybrid strategy: Let local centrality expose a topology blind spot and global subgroup methods expose a complexity cost before proposing a bounded combination.

a network description is converted into ranked decision outputs: Move from mixed labeled and unlabeled people to a descending priority list and a separate leader decision, then name the operational reason for both.
human reasoning limits motivate machine assistance: Acknowledge the human reasoning action, expose its scale limit, and assign the machine a narrow role that preserves expert judgment.

a behavioral observation becomes a measurable feature: State an interaction tendency, compare it with an opposing group, define a graph or message feature, and explain the direction of its expected effect.
small labeled data trigger leave-one-out validation: State the 15-label constraint, reserve one case at a time, average all rounds, and keep training and held-out errors distinct.

validation error triggers a semantic model repair: Report the base error, identify information the topology misses, construct a semantic feature mechanism, retrain, and compare under the same stated error measure.
human semantic clues seed an expert dictionary: Show a concrete word-level analogy, admit lexical ambiguity, retain detector reasoning, and formalize only the repeatable part as a dictionary.

two-stage resource allocation produces a topic rank: Initialize known topics, allocate resource to dictionary words, return it to topics, interpret the final amount as similarity, and read the ranked table.

likelihood is separated from leadership before a model switch: State that classification likelihood is not proportional to leadership, name the topology requirement, and switch to a ranking model on a filtered subgraph.

domain direction mismatch triggers edge reversal: Compare what an edge means in the source algorithm and target communication graph, state the leadership premise, and reverse edges to restore semantic compatibility.

a leader rank is cross-checked against a centrality pattern: Name the ranked candidate, plot degree against betweenness, compare with an empirical leader profile, and phrase the match as support rather than independent proof.

network defects and decision harms motivate sensitivity analysis: Name incompleteness and inconsistency, state the accusation or omission harm, introduce changed information, and rerun the full method.

rank changes are summarized by a metric and then stress-tested: Show concrete top-list movement, define Kendall's tau, report the observed value, vary label error, and read the curve at a policy-relevant endpoint.

a scatter plot distinguishes rank stability from probability inflation: Put old probability on one axis and new probability on the other, inspect displacement from the diagonal, and connect the common upward shift to expanded suspicious evidence.

portability is bounded by shared structure and different mechanisms: List transferable network regularities, then identify a domain mechanism that breaks the analogy and point to a domain-specific dynamics model.

source_quality.summary: Text extraction is complete; all 20 pages were read and visually reviewed. Summary and literal Introduction are present, no separate Abstract exists, and Contents/References are excluded from positive language. Label, feature, fold, semantic, direction, formula, calibration, leader, sensitivity, and transfer defects remain explicit warnings.

title: Finding Conspirators in the Network: Machine Learning with Resource-allocation Dynamics
unresolved_questions: The official task statement is unavailable, so task requirements are reconstructed only from the paper's Summary and internal Requirement references.
Summary claims of 73% and 87% correct rates, tau 0.86, and a named leader are paper-internal results without independent reproduction.
The linear-separability premise for conspirators and non-conspirators is asserted without a diagnostic, margin analysis, or alternative classifier.
Network stability over a long period is assumed even though message time, organizational change, and label timing are not modeled.
The EZ and 83-node networks are assumed to share an information-transmission mechanism without a transportability test.
Behavioral assumptions about conspirators, outsiders, irrelevant topics, leader contacts, and non-conspirator knowledge can encode investigator expectations into features.
The three centrality normalizations and shortest-path conventions are not reconciled with disconnected nodes, direction, ties, or standard alternative definitions.
Known-neighbor and known-conspirator-message features reuse labeled nodes and can leak label proximity into both fitting and evaluation.
Topic 16 is discarded as wrong without a versioned correction log, source reason, denominator effect, or sensitivity rerun.
The paper alternates between gradient ascent and gradient descent language and supplies no code, convergence tolerance, scaling, seed, or coefficient table.
The internal logistic score is called a probability without calibration, uncertainty, class threshold, or cost-sensitive decision rule.
Only 15 labeled nodes are available; leave-one-out variance, label composition, class balance, and fold-specific predictions are not reported.
Regularization is selected on the same leave-one-out process used to report error, without nested model selection or an external test set.
Zero training error with a small labeled set is reported without an overfitting, coefficient-stability, or feature-ablation analysis.
The manager identity choice uses the larger out-degree among duplicate names, a post hoc identity rule that can change the plotted interpretation.
The semantic dictionary is hand-built from known suspicious messages, so vocabulary leakage, lexical ambiguity, annotator disagreement, and drift are unmeasured.
Resource-allocation notation and index direction are ambiguous, and the equations omit tokenization, word counts, repeated terms, normalization, and empty-degree cases.
The error drop from 0.27 to 0.13 follows feature discovery and retraining on the same 15 labels; the enhancement is not nested or independently held out.
The prose says topic 4 is appended even though Table 3 places topics 1,3,4,6,8,9,10,14 at similarity zero, creating an unresolved result-to-action inconsistency.
The O(n) complexity claim excludes expert-dictionary construction, text preprocessing, graph creation, analyst review, memory, and the source's own large-noise bottleneck.
The displayed LeaderRank update multiplies by v_i(t) rather than an explicitly indexed neighbor score; the source notation is retained but not silently repaired.
The suspicious-topic subgraph condition uses unclear set-containment notation and does not define messages with multiple topics or empty intersections.
Every communication edge is reversed under the untested premise that a criminal leader sends commands rather than receives reports or delegates through intermediaries.
Adding a ground node and reversing edges alter topology; convergence, manipulation robustness, and parameter-free behavior are cited rather than reproduced on this graph.
Yao's LeaderRank result is cross-checked with degree and betweenness computed on the same network and a literature heuristic, not an independent leader label.
Kendall tau 0.86 measures rank agreement, while Table 5 and Figure 7 show material probability movement; rank stability is not probability calibration or action stability.
The label-error stress curve assumes independent wrong classifications, gives no simulation protocol or uncertainty interval, and does not test correlated or adversarial errors.
The paper admits feature non-portability and dictionary construction failure at scale; no external network, runtime, privacy, ethics, false-positive cost, or deployment validation is supplied.

writing_logic.summary: network task -> assumptions -> classifier and semantic enhancement -> leader model -> numerical checks -> limitations
mixed labeled/unlabeled network -> descending priority list -> separate leader output -> law-enforcement attention
local centrality blind spot -> global SNA complexity -> hybrid local learning and low-cost dynamics
human deduction -> scale failure -> machine assistance -> retained semantic judgment
behavioral contrast -> graph/message feature -> expected score direction -> classifier input
15 labels -> 14/1 folds -> mean held-out error -> lambda selection -> full-data retrain
word-level clue -> lexical ambiguity -> expert dictionary -> bipartite semantic representation
known-topic resource -> dictionary words -> return to topics -> similarity rank -> classifier feedback
classifier likelihood -> not leadership -> topology estimand -> filtered LeaderRank switch
SNS follow edge -> communication send edge -> command-sender premise -> edge reversal
LeaderRank candidate -> degree/betweenness plot -> empirical profile -> qualified support
network incompleteness -> accusation/omission harm -> changed labels/topics -> full sensitivity rerun
concrete rank movement -> Kendall tau -> independent-error curve -> endpoint reading
old probability -> new probability -> diagonal displacement -> evidence-compatible inflation
shared network regularities -> portability opportunity -> transmission-mechanism difference -> domain-specific model
